name: SequoiaDB
tagline: Chinese distributed document database with native ACID storage, SQL instances and S3 API, used in many banks.
description: SequoiaDB is a distributed database from Guangzhou-based SequoiaDB Corporation, first released in 2013 and open-sourced in 2014. Its core is a natively distributed, JSON document storage engine with full ACID transactions, sharding, multi-replica high availability and elastic scale-out; on top of it the company layers SQL instances compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL, an S3-compatible object interface and a file-system gateway, which it markets as multi-model. The vendor reports production use in more than 100 banks and clusters of up to 500 servers and 3 PB, mainly for historical-data platforms, real-time data hubs and content management in Chinese financial services. In July 2025 the main repository moved to a new GitHub home and was relicensed from AGPL-3.0 to Apache 2.0; development of the 5.x line continues.

pricing.notes: Open-source engine with a free download; commercial enterprise editions and support from SequoiaDB Corporation.

scale.notes: Vendor cites clusters of up to 500 physical servers and about 3 PB, with remote disaster-recovery replication.

strengths: Native distributed document engine with full ACID transactions
MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible SQL instances over the same data
S3-compatible object storage and file gateway in one platform
Proven in large Chinese banking deployments
Now under the permissive Apache 2.0 license
weaknesses: Documentation and community are mostly in Chinese
Small ecosystem outside China; few managed offerings
Multi-layer architecture (engine plus SQL instances) adds operational complexity
useCases: Historical and full-volume data platforms in banking
Real-time data hubs combining JSON and SQL access
Content and image management with an S3-compatible API
Mainframe offload of read-heavy financial data
